title: inflections@1: one language's inflection tables
description: languages/<id>/inflections.jsonl. The first line is the header; every later line is one word (a lemma) with the forms it takes. A translator reads it both ways: a form found in text leads back to its lemma and features (行きました is go with @polite and @past), and a lemma with features leads to the form to write.

language.description: The language id; must match the folder.

notes.description: How the tables are written: which forms, which readings, where they come from.

lemma.description: The dictionary form, as the language's word lists write it.

reading.description: The lemma's romanization or kana, as in the language's matrix column.

m.description: The content meaning (meaning@1 id) the word carries.

class.description: The inflection class, named the way learners of the language know it (godan, ichidan, irregular).

forms.description: Every form listed for the word. One of them is named dictionary and is the lemma itself.

name.description: What learners call the form (dictionary, polite, te, stem), unique within the word.

features.description: Meaning@1 ids the form adds to the lemma's meaning: grammar meanings such as @past and @polite, or content meanings such as not. Empty for a form that adds none by itself (a stem or te form).
